## P02 — Azure Configuration, Secrets & Entra App Registration <a id="phase-azure-configuration"></a>

Provision and wire the only permitted Azure resources (one App Configuration store with local-dev and production labels, two Key Vaults, Entra app registrations) so the API and web app boot their configuration securely in both environments with refresh, feature flags and a local fallback.

## P03 — Backend Platform Kernel <a id="phase-backend-platform"></a>

Build the compact shared kernel that user management and every later module plug into before any business feature is written: module contract, persistence conventions and domain primitives, application primitives, HTTP/OpenAPI conventions, transport security, rate limiting and health, observability, migration tooling, and the attachments building block; background jobs and the outbox are deferred to `business-building-blocks` to keep the path to first deployment short.

Id `backend-platform` · Milestone: M1 Platform foundations · Status: ⏳ in progress · Depends on: `azure-configuration`

  - Note: ADR-0020 and docs/guides/observability.md: metrics from the explicit TelemetryMeters.Names list (ASP.NET Core hosting, Kestrel, memory pool, routing, diagnostics, rate limiting, authentication, authorization, System.Net.Http, name resolution, System.Runtime, Dewiride.Erp.*), plus Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore, SqlClient db.client.operation.duration and Polly; OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Runtime removed. AddErpDatabaseTelemetry (Persistence) adds SqlClient spans with command text and no parameter values, and SqlErrorStatusProcessor clears the error message SQL Server can quote a value in. ErpResourceDetector reports the host version and deployment environment. CA1848 and CA2254 are errors. AddErpHttpClientDefaults (in AddErpPlatform) gives every IHttpClientFactory client the standard resilience handler, retries only for safe methods and one pipeline per destination; Polly 8.8.0 approved by the owner and pinned. Verified in the local Aspire dashboard: the startups request trace with its SQL span, and the SQL log carrying the caller's correlation id.

Deviations: no per-context bundles and no ef.ps1/ef.sh (ADR-0021); the local erp_local_migrator SQL login was created with the owner's consent.
- [ ] **P03.10** Attachments building block (`backend-platform-attachments-building-block`) — ⏳ in progress since 2026-09-26 <a id="backend-platform-attachments-building-block"></a>
  Add backend/BuildingBlocks/Attachments with an IDocumentStore abstraction backed by an encrypted, content-addressed Docker volume, metadata in a `files` schema, size and content-type allow-list, virus-scan hook interface, authorised time-limited download endpoint, upload endpoint and a frontend/packages/ui upload component, so every business module stores real files from day one and `documents` extends rather than replaces it.
  - POST /api/platform/attachments streams one multipart file into Erp:Platform:Attachments:RootPath as an AES-256-GCM envelope under a per-file data key wrapped by the configured key-encryption key, records it in the files schema, stores identical content once, and answers 413 over MaxSizeBytes, 415 for a content type outside the allow-list or whose leading bytes do not match it and 400 for an empty file, as ProblemDetails, without leaving a file behind
  - A download link from POST /api/platform/attachments/{id}/download-links streams the original bytes with the original file name and content type until DownloadLinkLifetime passes; a tampered, expired, other-actor or deleted-attachment link answers 404, and a stored file whose envelope fails authentication answers 404 before any byte is sent
  - The virus-scan hook runs on every upload: without a scanner the attachment records NotScanned, a clean verdict records Clean, and an infected verdict answers 422 attachment.infected and stores nothing
  - The web /platform/attachments page uploads through the shared drop-zone component with progress, lists, downloads and deletes attachments, refuses an oversized or disallowed file before sending it, and is covered by Playwright on desktop and mobile in light and dark with screenshots, including the disabled-flag state
  - ADR-0022 records the envelope format, the key source and rotation, the storage layout and the download-link design, and the encryption key is wired for local development, the containers, CI and production with owner-created secrets and consented seeding

## P07 — First On-Prem Deployment <a id="phase-first-deployment"></a>

Take API, web app, migrator and reverse proxy live on the Ubuntu home server with Docker Compose, TLS, secrets, health gating, backups and a repeatable, attestation-verified deployment pipeline; closes M3 with user management as the only business module.

Id `first-deployment` · Milestone: M3 First on-prem deployment · Status: planned · Depends on: `user-management`

- [ ] **P07.1** Production compose stack (`first-deployment-production-compose-stack`) <a id="first-deployment-production-compose-stack"></a>
  Complete infra/compose/compose.yaml and compose.production.yaml with proxy, api, web and one-shot migrator services, named volumes (data-protection keys, attachments, proxy certificates), hardened settings (read_only with tmpfs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, resource limits, log rotation, restart unless-stopped, healthcheck on every service, depends_on service_healthy), file-backed secrets for the service-principal certificate, profiles so SQL Server never starts in production, and `docker compose config` validation in CI.
  - Note: From backend-platform-transport-security-middleware: the API is called under three host names in production - the public host name (the edge proxy routes /api/* straight to api:8080 and passes the browser's Host through), api (the web container's server-side calls to http://api:8080) and 127.0.0.1 (the container health probe) - so the production value of Erp:Platform:Host:AllowedHosts is <public host name>;api;127.0.0.1, and Erp:Platform:Host:KnownNetworks must list the compose network so forwarded client addresses are trusted; an empty list trusts no proxy. Never set ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED. From backend-platform-attachments-building-block: the api service stores encrypted attachments under Erp:Platform:Attachments:RootPath=/var/erp/attachments on the named volume attachments, which lands in Docker's data root on the server's system drive by default; ask the owner which drive holds attachments (the volume can be bound to a mount on a second disk through driver options without a code change) before the stack goes live, and keep the volume writable while the container root stays read_only.
- [ ] **P07.2** Production database provisioning (`first-deployment-production-database-provisioning`) <a id="first-deployment-production-database-provisioning"></a>
  Provision Azure SQL (serverless free offer or small provisioned tier, recorded as an ADR) with an Entra admin, contained users for the app (data role) and migrator (schema role), service-principal connection strings stored in Key Vault, firewall rules for the home server, the free-amount-remaining alert, and a documented fallback to a SQL Server Express container.
  - Note: From backend-platform-migration-tooling-and-seeding (ADR-0021): create the migrator service principal (certificate file erp-migrator-client.pem, id in MIGRATOR_AZURE_CLIENT_ID) with App Configuration Data Reader and Key Vault Secrets User on the production store and vault, its contained database user with the schema role, the secret Erp--Platform--Database--MigratorConnectionString in kv-erp-ai-pro-prod and its production-label reference Erp:Platform:Database:MigratorConnectionString; compose.production.yaml already runs the migrator service with that identity.
- [ ] **P07.3** Host bootstrap runbook and scripts (`first-deployment-host-bootstrap-runbook-and-scripts`) <a id="first-deployment-host-bootstrap-runbook-and-scripts"></a>
  Write docs/runbooks/host-setup.md and infra/compose/host scripts for Ubuntu hardening (unattended upgrades, ufw, fail2ban, SSH keys only), Docker Engine install, non-root deploy user, mounted service-principal certificate, .env for non-secret values, DNS and router port-forwarding, and a systemd unit running `docker compose up -d --wait`.
- [ ] **P07.4** Reverse proxy and TLS (`first-deployment-reverse-proxy-and-tls`) <a id="first-deployment-reverse-proxy-and-tls"></a>
  Configure the edge proxy (Caddy with automatic TLS as default, nginx+certbot as alternative, recorded as an ADR) routing /api/* to api:8080 and everything else to web:3000, TLS 1.2+, HSTS ramp-up, forwarded headers with KnownIPNetworks equal to the compose subnet, security headers, request size limits, streaming buffering off and no host-published ports other than 80/443, verified by a local end-to-end run through the proxy including the Entra redirect flow.
  - Note: From backend-platform-rate-limiting-output-caching-and-health (ADR-0019): the edge proxy must append the client address to X-Forwarded-For on requests it passes to both the API and the web container, because the web container forwards the last entry on its server-side API calls and the API rate-limits anonymous callers by it; the web container must be reachable only through the proxy.
- [ ] **P07.5** Release and deploy pipeline (`first-deployment-release-and-deploy-pipeline`) <a id="first-deployment-release-and-deploy-pipeline"></a>
  Add a release workflow on v* tags building and pushing images with SBOM, provenance, attestations and the CVE gate, and host-side deploy.sh and rollback.sh that pull by digest, run `gh attestation verify`, execute the migrator, roll api/web with health-gated cutover, prune, and roll back to the previous digest on failure, with a shellcheck CI job.
  - Note: From backend-platform-migration-tooling-and-seeding (ADR-0021): the migrator ships inside the api image at /app/migrator as the compose migrator service (pull_policy never, restart no). docker compose up recreates a changed api container before it evaluates the api depends_on condition service_completed_successfully, so deploy.sh must pull api and web, run docker compose run --rm migrator on its own, stop and keep the running api when it exits non-zero, and only then run up -d --remove-orphans --wait. Migrator exit codes: 0 succeeded, 1 failed or cancelled, 2 configuration could not be loaded or is invalid, 3 migrations pending (status), 64 usage. docs/operations/runbooks/migrations.md is the manual form of this sequence.
- [ ] **P07.6** Health probes and uptime monitoring (`first-deployment-health-probes-and-uptime-monitoring`) <a id="first-deployment-health-probes-and-uptime-monitoring"></a>
  Provide a shell-less health probe for the chiseled API image (tiny .NET probe entrypoint or proxy-side active checks), a /api/health route in the web app, compose healthcheck definitions and an external uptime monitor hitting /healthz/live through the proxy with alerting to the owner.
- [ ] **P07.7** Backups and restore drill (`first-deployment-backups-and-restore-drill`) <a id="first-deployment-backups-and-restore-drill"></a>
  Verify Azure SQL automated backups and PITR retention, back up the data-protection key volume, attachments volume and compose configuration nightly to an encrypted off-host location, and rehearse a full restore documented in docs/runbooks/restore.md with measured RTO/RPO.
- [ ] **P07.8** Go-live checklist and production smoke (`first-deployment-go-live-checklist-and-production-smoke`) <a id="first-deployment-go-live-checklist-and-production-smoke"></a>
  Run a production Playwright smoke project (real Entra test user via stored auth state, users list renders, sign-out) against the live URL, confirm traces and logs arrive, complete docs/runbooks/go-live-checklist.md, record ADR deployment topology, and mark milestone M3 done in the roadmap.
